releases.title: Core editor and ribbon workspace
releases.summary: A consolidated release of the user-verified editor: crisp vector display, live editing, grouped ribbons, object controls and compact properties.

Added: Home, Tool Settings, Export and Advanced Settings ribbons with persistent Favorites and tool ordering.
Objects pane with descriptive labels, drag stacking, visibility and locking.
Raster Preview, Fit to Screen, automatic transparent canvas growth and trimming, and rotate handles.
Independent Step outlines, underline and strikethrough, shared format painting and live mixed-selection text formatting.
Improved: Inline Text properties for shapes, callouts and Steps with Back to Object; color controls update live and saved colors support Update/Remove.
Consistent grouped Quick Styles, custom-style popup, live creation previews and remembered formatting.
Stable corner handles and continuous rounding, first-object alignment with canvas expansion, Crop panning and zooming, and compact footer controls.
Property instructions are in circled-question-mark header tooltips; Selection actions have distinct icons.
Verified: All64 accumulated manual checks passed by the user across the recorded candidate builds; exact tested-build attribution is preserved.
364 automated Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy; synthetic egui interaction and render fixtures.
Exact optimized export/viewport/previous-fixture equality, portable projects, Undo and existing Library persistence checks.

limitations: Clipboard paste into the current canvas, Simplify, persistent groups and additional selection masks remain unfinished.
Text outlines, per-object shadows, advanced Line/Arrow configuration and additional typography options are still planned or in development.
Two bundled font families and basic left-to-right text layout; system fonts and mixed styling within one text box are not yet available.
This unsigned Windows alpha retains the existing Library capacity and capture qualification limitations.

releases.title: Editable Library autosave
releases.summary: Keep your original image and editable annotations automatically, including inline text drafts. Close and resume from the Library without a Save As detour.

Added: Background Library checkpoints after750ms without changes, or after2seconds of continuous typing. One writer coalesces rapid edits; saved text drafts do not split Undo transactions.
Timestamped Library names and stable item identities. Reopening an image edits the same item, and Undo/Redo changes save automatically.
Saved to Library status, explicit retry after write failure, and a close/switch barrier that waits for the latest revision. Successful persistence needs no save prompt.
Improved: New immutable revision files and an atomic index protect the last saved state. Conflicting writes from another editor are rejected.
Library capacity failures preserve older images. Save As remains available for an additional portable project copy.
Verified: Native inline draft checkpoint, close without prompt, restart/reopen with all objects, exact clipboard output, real lock failure and retry, and one-step Undo persistence.
214Rust tests cover debounce timing, edits during background writes, source/annotation preservation, stale windows, failed writes, limits and document switching.

limitations: The Library currently holds up to50images within512MB. When full, new saves fail visibly; use Save As. Configurable limits and Library deletion management remain unfinished.
Library index version2 is required for editable revisions. Earlier ClipCraft versions cannot open this updated Library; portable project JSON remains compatible with its supported objects.
The checkpoint interval is not a promise of zero loss during power failure. Wait for Saved to Library before relying on the latest checkpoint.
Full core-tool options, Simplify, crisp vector zoom and toolbar ordering remain incomplete.

releases.title: Text fitting and compact formatting controls
releases.summary: Control text overflow and wrapping, with a compact row for alignment, distribution, justification and everyday text formatting.

Added: Advanced text fitting: Do not autofit, Shrink text on overflow and Resize shape to fit text. New text defaults to shrinking on overflow; older projects keep their previous layout.
Wrap text in shape checkbox. Wrapped shape fitting keeps width and fits height; unwrapped fitting adjusts width and height to the text lines.
One compact icon row under Alignment & Distribution and Quick Text Settings, with full-name hover labels and remembered enclosed dropdown choices.
Working Bold, Italic, Increase font size and Decrease font size buttons with selection-wide edits and active state. Real licensed font variants are shared by inline editing and export.
Fitting, wrapping, bold and italic persist in saved templates and editable projects. Live shape resizing and inline text use the shared document layout.
Verified: Native fitting modes, wrapping, bold/italic, geometry Undo/Redo and exact clipboard output; automated template, batch, invalid-input, persistence and multi-zoom caret checks.
The user confirmed all four alpha47 modifier workflows pass physical testing: Alt duplication, Alt centered resize, Shift proportions and Shift+Alt combined, each with one-step Undo.

limitations: Do not autofit clips overflowing text to the content box. Resize shape rejects a result larger than the canvas; choose Shrink or enlarge the canvas instead.
Text formatting applies to the whole object. Mixed formatting within a text box, underline and text effects remain planned.
Full core-tool options, Simplify, crisp vector zoom, editable Library autosave and toolbar ordering remain unfinished.

releases.title: Optional tool switching and flexible resize handles
releases.summary: Choose whether clicking another object changes tools, and resize height or width independently with new edge handles.

Added: Edit > Automatically switch tools when selecting objects. This saved setting is off by default; enable it to select another annotation type and activate its tool and properties in one click.
Top, bottom, left and right midpoint handles alongside the existing corners. Ordinary edge drags preserve the other dimension, redraw live and commit with one Undo.
Preview: Alt-drag object bodies or selected groups to duplicate with live previews and one Undo. Alt on a handle instead resizes around the center.

Shift preserves resize proportions; Shift+Alt combines proportions with center resizing. Shift constrains line endpoints to 45-degree steps. These gestures pass automated input tests; physical held-key drag verification remains pending.
Verified: Native tool switching on/off, preference retention after restart, independent height resizing, one-step Undo/Redo and exact clipboard output from a reopened editable fixture.
Automated copying tests cover all 14 annotation kinds, selected groups, fresh identities, original preservation, snapping, persistence and atomic Undo.

limitations: The desktop inspection API cannot hold modifier keys during a drag. Alt-drag duplication and Shift/Alt resize remain flagged for physical gesture verification in the roadmap.
Complete core-tool options, Simplify, crisp vector zoom, editable autosave and toolbar ordering remain unfinished.
Movement and Step placement have object alignment snapping. Resize-to-object, grid and constrained new drawing remain pending.

releases.title: Quick Styles that remember your choices
releases.summary: Choose a style family, repeat its last variation in one click, and manage saved styles directly from their tiles.

Added: Compact grouped Quick Styles for Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Circle / ellipse, Other shapes, Text / Monospace, Callout / Rounded Callout and currently supported straight arrows. Saved styles appear first.
Each category keeps its last variation across restarts. Its main preview repeats that choice; an enclosed triangle opens the variations.
Right-click a saved style to Update from selection or Delete style. Updating retains its name; neither action changes other document objects.
Presets and saved templates also set new-object formatting. Shape category changes preserve selected labels, bounds and identities with one Undo.
Verified: Native saved-style update/delete, repeated preset changes, saved-first ordering, active borders, and main-button repetition after process restart.
Editable shape conversion and new styled drawing preserve original image data; native clipboard output matches256000pixels.

limitations: Only implemented geometry is offered: Other contains the current polygon; callouts use the current box/tail geometry; curved arrows remain planned.
Complete core-tool options, Simplify, crisp vector zoom, editable autosave and toolbar ordering remain unfinished.
Snapping covers object/group movement and new Step placement. Drawing endpoints, resizing, grid and angle snapping remain pending.

releases.title: Place, align and keep editing
releases.summary: Drag new Steps into position, snap object edges and centers, and see which objects your current tool can edit.

Added: New Steps appear on mouse-down and follow the held pointer until release. One Undo removes the marker and restores its sequence number.
Canvas Snapping in the Image menu aligns moving objects, groups and new Steps to other objects' edges and centers. The toggle is remembered.
Compatible objects show a cyan border and nodes on hover. Newly drawn annotations stay selected for immediate property edits.
Improved: Alignment, distribution, text justification and Capture use an enclosing control with a filled triangle dropdown. Last-used arrangement actions still repeat from the main button.
Verified: Native Step dragging, retained selection, Undo/Redo and numbering, editable reopen and256000exact clipboard pixels.
Native snapping enabled/disabled yields exact center positions320/317. Local input checks cover different zooms and actual guide painting, group geometry, persistence and one Undo.

limitations: Grouped style categories and saved-first style ordering remain in progress; circular curved arrows remain planned.
Snapping currently covers object/group movement and new Step placement. Drawing endpoints, resizing, angle/grid snapping and broader workspace preferences remain unfinished.
Simplify, advanced core-tool options, smooth vector display, editable autosave and toolbar reordering remain in the roadmap.

releases.title: Type in place and compare annotations
releases.summary: Type directly inside text boxes, callouts and shapes, with sidebar formatting and a one-click annotation comparison view.

Added: Direct canvas text entry replaces the popup. Draw a text box or callout and type; double-click rectangles, ellipses and polygons to add editable text.
New text uses horizontal center and vertical middle. Old saved alignments stay intact. Shape labels support a text color independent of the outline.
Use sidebar formatting while typing. Click outside or press Ctrl+Enter to finish; one Undo restores the previous label and formatting.
Hide annotations / Show annotations beside Show Recent compares the current underlying image without changing saved objects, selection, clipboard or exported images.
Tool-aware canvas pointers show the active tool and switch to move, resize and pan feedback for the current interaction.
Verified: Native inline typing in Text, Callout, Rectangle, Ellipse and Polygon objects, sidebar formatting, one Undo, editable save and a fresh process reopen.
Independent saved-object checks preserve original image data and existing geometry. Clipboard comparisons verify complete output, including when annotations are hidden.
Local input regressions cover keyboard selection, cancellation, invalid input, legacy alignment, tool pointer priority and view-only annotation comparison.
Shared layout regression covers both fonts, five widths, four zoom levels, tabs, CRLF and blank lines. Native Package wrapping stays unchanged on commit and one Undo restores the original.
Fixed: Inline typing and exported text now use the same wrapping and caret metrics. Borderline words retain their line breaks when an edit is committed, at every canvas zoom.

limitations: Grouped style dropdowns, saved-first ordering and unified split buttons with remembered previews are next. Circular curved arrows remain planned.
Hide annotations hides current editable overlays. It cannot separate objects already merged by earlier explicit flatten, crop or fill operations; nondestructive image operations remain planned.
Text uses two bundled fonts and basic left-to-right wrapping. Rich text and exact high-zoom vector display remain unfinished.
Simplify, complete core-tool options, smooth callout joins, continuous editable autosave and toolbar dragging remain in the roadmap.

releases.title: Save and reuse object formatting
releases.summary: Save a selected object's formatting as a local template, then apply it to matching objects with one click.

Added: Working Quick Styles for Text, Line, Step, rectangles, ellipses, polygons and callouts, plus intensity presets for Blur and Pixelate.
Save as template captures one selected object's formatting. Use an automatic name or enter your own; templates persist locally across restarts.
Click any preset or saved template to update a compatible selection immediately. The active tile has a visible border, and one Undo reverses the batch.
Templates retain each object's position, size, paths, callout pointer and individual text. Existing arrow styles remain available.
Verified: Native repeated callout preset changes, custom save and batch application, active borders and one-step Undo passed.
Native Text, Line, Rectangle, Step, Ellipse, Polygon, Blur and Pixelate presets produce eight independently checked editable objects and 256000 exact clipboard pixels.
Local checks cover atomic batch application, no-op history, content/geometry preservation, persistence, malformed data and locked storage.

limitations: The new templates apply to existing objects of exactly one type. They do not yet set defaults for newly drawn objects. Arrow drawing defaults retain their existing behavior.
Simplify and advanced tool options remain unfinished. Text entry is still dialog-based; inline centered text in shapes, text boxes and callouts is the next priority.
Template tiles show a type/color glyph rather than a complete preview of every formatting property.
Crisp vector zoom, smooth callout joins, continuous editable autosave and draggable toolbar ordering remain tracked. Physical middle-button drag verification is pending.

releases.title: Remembered alignment, spacing and text controls
releases.summary: Arrange selected objects and justify their text from upper-right split buttons that remember your choices.

Added: Seven object alignment actions, including centering both axes, and four horizontal/vertical distribution actions for equal centers or equal gaps.
Nine text justification combinations, including center/middle, applied together to selected text-capable objects while preserving their individual labels.
Dropdown choices apply immediately and become the main button's displayed icon and label. Click the main button to repeat that action on another selection.
Alignment, distribution and text choices are saved independently in local preferences across app restarts. Inapplicable actions are disabled.
Verified: Native callout alignment, equal vertical gaps, centered and bottom-right text, one-step Undo, editable save and 256000 clipboard pixels passed on synthetic content.
Engine checks cover all alignment/distribution actions, fractional coordinates, invalid inputs, persistence, no-op history and atomic preference storage.
Bounds algorithms adapt audited MIT DesignCraft code; ClipCraft document commands and UI remain independent.

limitations: Alignment uses selected object bounds, including callout pointers. Key-object/page alignment, persistent groups and group rotation remain unfinished.
Text entry still uses the existing dialog. Inline centered text and shape text, reusable templates beyond arrows, crisp vector zoom, editable autosave and toolbar ordering remain priority work.
Middle-button panning passes input tests but still needs a physical held-middle-button drag check. It has no Ready claim.
This unsigned Windows alpha does not claim complete Snagit UI or behavior parity.

releases.title: Select, move and format objects together
releases.summary: Select existing objects with their own tool, move selections together and change shared formatting in one undoable edit.

Added: The active annotation tool selects matching existing objects and their handles. Clicking a Step selects it without making another marker or advancing its sequence.
Shift-click adds or removes objects from a selection. Select same type collects matching objects; Ctrl+A selects all with Move or the active tool's matching objects.
Drag or nudge selected objects together with shared edge limits and one Undo. Delete removes the selected objects together.

Selected objects of the same type share live color, stroke, fill and text-formatting edits. Individual text, labels and geometry remain intact. Existing arrow presets also apply across selected arrows.
Fixed: Preserve fast canvas drags whose press and release arrive between rendered frames.
Verified: Native Step selection, group movement, live color preview, commit, Undo/Redo and editable save passed on original synthetic content.
All eight saved objects match expected data; only the three selected Step colors changed. Native Copy All matches all 256000 image pixels.
Local tests cover typed hit testing, Shift selection, group movement, batch formatting, atomic invalid-input rollback, no-op Redo preservation and editable persistence.

limitations: Middle-mouse panning is implemented and passes egui input tests; physical middle-drag verification remains pending. It has no Ready claim yet.
Mixed-type selections can move together; shared formatting requires one object type. Persistent groups, group resizing/rotation and reusable presets beyond arrows remain unfinished.
Remembered contextual alignment/distribution buttons, inline centered text, crisp vector zoom, continuous editable autosave and draggable toolbar ordering are priority follow-ups.
This unsigned Windows alpha does not claim complete Snagit UI or behavior parity.

releases.title: Horizontal and vertical Cut Out
releases.summary: Remove an unwanted strip, preview the joined image as you drag, and undo the cut in one step.

Added: More > Cut Out removes straight horizontal or vertical strips with either drag direction.
The canvas previews the joined image using existing texture slices. Plain images commit on mouse release; editable objects show a flattening review with Cancel.
One Undo restores the prior dimensions, pixels and editable objects. Projects retain the original image for Revert.
Verified: Native horizontal review/Cancel/apply and vertical release commit, Undo/Redo and save passed on synthetic content.
A combined 80-pixel horizontal and 150-pixel vertical cut matched all156800 saved pixels against an independent array comparison.
Engine tests cover exact RGBA at both joins and image edges, one-pixel survivors, invalid strips, preserved Redo, save/reopen and original restoration.
Shortcut eligibility is tested during drag, flatten review and idle Cut Out, preserving keyboard Undo after release.

limitations: Straight edges only. Torn, wave, zigzag and reference preset matching remain unfinished.
Cutting an image with editable objects flattens them after review; Undo restores editability. The drag preview stays anchored to the original image until commit.
This unsigned Windows alpha does not claim complete Snagit behavior or interface parity.

releases.title: Rectangular pixel selection
releases.summary: Select a rectangle, adjust its handles, and copy, cut or clear the selected pixels with Undo.

Added: Selection now supports reverse dragging, bounded movement and eight resize handles, plus Select entire image and Deselect.
Copy selection preserves exact color and transparency. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Delete operate on the pixel selection; Copy All still copies the complete image.
Cut and Clear show a flattening review for editable objects. Cut copies successfully before clearing; one Undo restores pixels and objects.
Verified: Native reverse selection, movement, resizing, Copy/Cut, review Cancel, Undo/Redo and save passed on synthetic content.
All 129600 selected clipboard pixels and all 256000 saved image pixels match independent expected images, including transparency and unchanged pixels outside the selection.
Tests verify clipboard failure preserves editable objects, Undo/Redo history and image pixels.

limitations: This release selects rectangular pixels. Ellipse, polygon, lasso, inverse selection, Magic Wand, selection-constrained Fill and moving selected pixel content remain unfinished.
Moving the rectangle changes the selection only. Pixel edits flatten annotations after review; Undo restores them. Undo exits the transient selection mode.
This unsigned Windows alpha does not claim complete Snagit behavior or interface parity.

releases.title: Connected color fill
releases.summary: Click to fill a connected region with color and opacity, control matching tolerance, and undo the complete change.

Added: More > Fill provides color, opacity and tolerance controls for connected image regions.
Images with editable objects show a Flatten and fill review before applying; Cancel keeps the project unchanged.
One Undo restores pixels and editable objects. Filled projects retain original source pixels for Revert.
Verified: Native region selection, Cancel, translucent fill, Undo/Redo, save and actual clipboard output pass synthetic checks.
Independent flood filling matches all 256000 saved pixels, including 190762 changed background pixels.
Shared-engine tests cover barriers, diagonals, seed-relative tolerance, transparent colors, large regions, no-op history and persistence.

limitations: Fill operates on four-connected regions of the complete image. Selection masks, global replacement and antialiased fill remain unfinished.
Applying fill to annotations flattens them after review; Undo restores editability. Editable projects retain the original image.
This unsigned Windows alpha does not claim complete Snagit behavior or interface parity.

releases.title: Editable pixel eraser
releases.summary: Erase to transparency with a smooth brush, keep strokes editable, and restore a complete gesture with one Undo.

Added: More > Eraser supports click dots and freehand strokes across the image and earlier annotations.
Drawing previews actual transparent pixels. Width and opacity edits update the selected stroke live.
Move eraser strokes and resize their bounds; save editable projects or copy/export flattened transparent output.
Verified: Native stroke creation, one-step Undo/Redo, opacity drag, movement and saved output pass synthetic checks.
An independent alpha-mask calculation matches all 256000 saved pixels; the actual Windows clipboard matches the same image.
Engine checks cover transparent input, stroke crossings, edge clipping, stacking, original retention and invalid paths.

limitations: Smooth round brushes support widths from 1 to 32 pixels. Brush presets and a hard-edge antialias toggle are unfinished.
Erasers affect the image and objects below them in the stack. Editable projects retain original image pixels.
This unsigned Windows alpha does not claim complete Snagit interface or behavior parity.

releases.title: Editable Blur and Pixelation
releases.summary: Draw rectangular visual effects, change their intensity live, and keep regions editable when saving your project.

Added: More > Blur creates editable rectangular Blur or Pixelate regions.
Selected regions offer Type and live Intensity controls with one Undo per released adjustment.
Move and resize effect regions using their canvas handles; save and reopen them as editable objects.
Verified: Shared renderer handles transparency, stacked objects and unchanged pixels outside the effect region.
Native creation, type switching, intensity Undo/Redo, movement, resizing, saved projects and clipboard output pass synthetic checks.
Pixelation matches an independent block-average calculation across a complete saved image.

limitations: Visual effects are not a secure-redaction guarantee. Editable projects retain original pixels; use solid Redact and flattened export when appropriate.
Only rectangular effect regions are implemented. Ellipse regions, effect Quick Styles and Smart Redact remain unfinished.
This unsigned Windows alpha does not claim complete Snagit behavior or interface parity.

releases.title: Interactive rectangular crop
releases.summary: Drag a crop rectangle, move or resize its handles, then apply or cancel. One Undo restores your image and editable objects.

Added: Crop tool with eight handles, reverse-direction drawing, movement, thirds grid, live dimensions and outside shading.
Properties hide while cropping. Crop/Cancel controls stay near the selection; projects with objects show an explicit Flatten and crop action.
Verified: 130 Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy; exact transparent-pixel crop, source retention, invalid inputs, persistence, boundary clamping and draft cancellation.
Native reverse drag, move, resize, Cancel, one-step Undo/Redo, saved output and actual OS clipboard comparisons.

limitations: Applying crop flattens the complete composite. Undo restores the previous editable objects; non-destructive off-canvas object editing remains unfinished.
Trim, crop aspect presets, numeric crop entry, object rotation and grouping remain planned.
Unsigned Windows x64 alpha. Full Snagit UI/behavior parity is not claimed.

releases.title: Rotate and flip the complete image
releases.summary: Turn screenshots clockwise, counterclockwise or 180 degrees, and flip them horizontally or vertically with one-step Undo.

Added: Image > Rotate quarter and half turns, plus Arrange > Flip Image Horizontal/Vertical. Exact pixel mappings preserve transparency without resampling.
Flatten confirmation when objects are present. Cancel preserves the document; one Undo restores the editable objects and original dimensions.
Verified: 126 Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy. All five native saved outputs match independent pixel mappings across 1,280,000 pixels.
Original-source retention, no-op Redo, invalid input rollback, real save/reopen and native clipboard comparisons.

limitations: These commands transform the whole image and flatten editable objects after confirmation. Selected-object rotation and flips remain unfinished.
Custom image angles, grouping, interactive crop and full reference UI parity remain unfinished.
Unsigned Windows x64 alpha. Testing uses original synthetic fixtures; full Snagit behavioral parity is not claimed.

releases.title: Filled shapes and editable polygons
releases.summary: Fill rectangles and ellipses, draw polygons, and preview color, opacity and side-count changes on the object.

Added: Fill/No Fill for rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses and polygons, with independent RGBA color and opacity.
Editable polygons with 3–64 sides, live resizing and one-step Undo. Geometry is adapted from MIT-licensed DesignCraft with attribution.
Verified: 122 Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy; native Fill/No Fill, opacity and side-count Undo/Redo, live fill color, resizing and saved output.
Exact native clipboard comparisons plus real project save/reopen, alpha-compositing, invalid-input and old no-fill compatibility tests.

limitations: Rotation, per-corner rounding, stars, shadows, grouping and interactive crop remain unfinished.
Use alpha.31 or newer for projects containing polygons or general shape fills. Older builds may omit fills.
Unsigned Windows x64 alpha. Reference behavioral parity is not claimed; native tests use original synthetic fixtures.

releases.title: Live object properties and editable ellipses
releases.summary: See stroke, corner and color changes on the object while editing; undo each gesture once. Draw and resize editable ellipses.

Added: Editable outlined ellipses in the Shape selector, using attributed MIT-licensed DesignCraft geometry adapted to the shared ClipCraft engine.
Live selected-object width, corner-radius and color/fill previews. Color Apply commits once; Cancel restores the original.
Fixed: A property slider drag now creates one Undo step. Escape and focus loss cancel the preview, including the later mouse release.
Canceled color changes preserve existing Redo history and exact RGBA bytes.
Verified: 117 Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy; native ellipse draw/resize/Undo/reopen, width and radius sliders, color previews, fill Apply/Undo and saved output.
Intermediate rendered-pixel tests demonstrate live changes without modifying the committed document.

limitations: Rotation, polygons, general rectangle/ellipse fills, per-corner styles and shadows remain unfinished.
Use alpha.30 or newer to reopen projects containing ellipses. Full reference UI/behavioral parity is not claimed.
Unsigned Windows x64 alpha. Text entry uses its existing separate draft workflow.

releases.title: Core drawing tools and draggable rounded corners
releases.summary: Draw with Pen, Line and Highlighter, place numbered steps, and round rectangle or callout corners by dragging inward.

Added: Editable Pen, Line and translucent Highlighter with color, opacity, width, movement, resizing and one-gesture Undo.
Numbered or lettered circular steps with next/reset controls, editable labels, size and fill color.
Blue inset corner handles round rectangles and callouts directly while drawing tools remain selected. Drag outward to square them again; size and callout pointer stay fixed.
Session capture delays of 3, 5 or 10 seconds, with a native countdown and cancellation.
Fixed: Continuous arrow coverage removes diagonal seams and composites overlapping segments once.
Verified: 112 Rust tests plus native creation, corner dragging, label editing, sequence reset, Undo, save and exact clipboard checks.
768000 native pixels across drawing, arrows and delayed capture; final optimized reopening and release roundtrip checks accompany the package.
Planning: Original missed roadmap targets stay visible. Unscheduled work no longer receives automatically rolled-forward release numbers. Partial releases are labeled explicitly.

limitations: Per-corner radii, additional shape families, advanced stroke presets and pen pressure remain unfinished.
Step markers currently use circles and automatic text contrast; alternative shapes and independent text color remain planned.
Use alpha.29 or newer for projects containing these new tools or corner radii. Full Snagit interface and behavioral parity are not claimed.
This is an unsigned Windows x64 alpha. Custom shortcuts, scrolling capture and persistent capture preferences remain planned.

releases.title: Arrow presets and saved custom styles
releases.summary: Reuse original arrow presets or save your own color, opacity and width settings locally.

Added: Eight original arrow presets in a four-column gallery, plus up to24 saved custom styles with names, RGBA color and width.
Save, refresh and right-click removal with local restart persistence; CLI style commands use the same storage and document engine.
Protected: Applying a style preserves endpoints and other objects, supports one-step Undo/Redo, and skips unchanged reapplications. Removing a preset leaves document history intact.
Atomic bounded storage protects against corrupt files, concurrent updates and invalid styles.
Fixed: Translucent arrows now composite over the background once per covered pixel, including overlapping shaft/head segments.
Verified: 100 regular Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy; native save/draw/restart/apply/remove and256000 exact clipboard pixels.
Independent source-over pixel colors and256000 CLI pixels, unchanged geometry and corruption/validation handling.

limitations: Thick diagonal arrow strokes still show seams; continuous stroke coverage is the next rendering milestone. Alternative and filled arrowheads remain planned.
Themes, favorites, other tool families and exact reference post-draw selection behavior remain unfinished.
Custom styles are stored locally. Preset removal does not change existing arrows or projects.

releases.title: Library sidebar, filters and thumbnail sizing
releases.summary: Browse local snapshots with year filters, four sort modes and adjustable thumbnails.

Added: Library sidebar with image counts and UTC year filters that combine with instant search.
Newest, oldest, name and stored-size sorting with deterministic tie breakers.
Independent 50–200% Library thumbnail sizing, a 100% reset and absolute UTC snapshot timestamps.
Improved: Recent tray hides during Library browsing and restores its previous visibility in Editor. The grid fits normal and minimum supported window sizes.
Verified: 95 regular Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy. Native filtering, sorting, sizing and unsaved protection pass.
Filtered editable-project reopen matches256000 exact clipboard pixels without modifying stored history.

limitations: Full reference date hierarchy, source groups, tags, list columns and batch export remain unfinished.
Video and step-capture categories are disabled. Browsing preferences currently last for the app session.
History snapshots are checkpoints; later edits require saving. Pin/close and per-edit recovery remain separate work.

releases.title: Compact recent tray and active snapshot
releases.summary: Browse compact thumbnails below the status row, with a clear active snapshot and protection for ongoing edits.

Improved: Compact recent cards now appear below the status row, with proportionate thumbnails, transparency checkerboards and image/project indicators.
Active-snapshot border, unsaved marker and stored-size tooltip make the current state clearer.
Protected: Reselecting the active thumbnail keeps edits and Undo history. Canceling a replacement preserves both the document and active selection.
Verified: Native selection, Cancel/Discard, Undo and exact320000 annotated/transparent clipboard pixels.
92 regular Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy. Reference close/Library retention observed with a synthetic canvas.

limitations: Pinning, per-item close, exact source-format badges, absolute timestamps and full reference tray behavior remain planned.
Thumbnails depict stored snapshots; later edits need saving. Per-edit recovery is separate work.

releases.title: Instant Library search
releases.summary: Find local snapshots by name, source and dimensions, then reopen an editable copy.

Added: Instant case-insensitive multiword Library search with matching counts, Clear and an empty-result message.
CLI history list --query uses the same matching rules.
Preserved: Refresh and returning to Library retain the session filter. Recent tray stays unfiltered, and searches leave stored snapshots untouched.
Verified: Native source/name/dimension filtering, Clear, no-results, refresh, recent tray and filtered recovery with256000 exact pixels.
91 regular Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy; nine CLI cases and unchanged history hashes.

limitations: Search text is session-only. Tags, folders, application/website navigation and full reference Library layout remain planned.
Matching is literal local metadata search; reference search semantics are not yet verified.

releases.title: Local history and editable recovery
releases.summary: Keep recent captures and saved revisions in a local Library, with thumbnails and editable snapshot recovery.

Added: Persistent local snapshots on opening, creating, pasting, capturing and explicit saving. Up to 50 snapshots and 512 MB of retained data.
Library thumbnails, recent-image tray and File > Open Recent reopen editable copies with unsaved-change protection.
Shared CLI history list, record and open commands.
Protected: Atomic index updates and a process lock merge snapshots from multiple windows. Missing or corrupt history leaves the open image intact.
Verified: Native revision recovery restores seven objects and matches all 256000 pixels; restart and missing-file recovery verified.
Real capture and Open Recent recovery each match 256000 synthetic pixels. 90 regular Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy.

limitations: Edits after the last snapshot require saving; per-edit recovery and retention preferences are planned.
Search, tags/folders, bulk import and full reference Library layout remain unfinished.
Expired snapshot deletion failures are reported and may leave files on disk; the open image remains intact.

releases.title: Compact New Image and canvas transparency
releases.summary: Create custom images in a compact dialog, with transparency and white canvas choices inside the color selector.

Improved: New Image follows the observed compact layout with right-aligned pixel fields, canvas swatch, title close and Create/Cancel footer.
Transparent and White canvas choices are available inside the color popup alongside exact RGBA/hex.
Fixed: Closing a nested color popup preserves the New Image draft. Outside clicks retain the modal; Escape cancels only the active layer.
Verified: Native invalid-size guard,320x200 transparent creation and64000 exact clipboard pixels; nested Escape preserves draft dimensions and the existing unsaved image.
86 regular Rust tests, formatting and strict Clippy. Reference Revert/Undo/Redo and576000 restored pixels observed; New Image picker controls added to the UI inventory.

limitations: Full reference canvas-picker, numeric validation, defaults and preference persistence remain unverified; the existing white default is preserved.

limitations: ClipCraft keeps the original image behind the warning; reference candidate-preview behavior and accepted reference filter output remain unverified.
Print units/DPI, selected-object flattening, interactive/off-canvas crop and complete reference UI parity remain unfinished.
Editable projects retain original source pixels; share flattened PNG output when originals should not be recoverable.

releases.title: Flatten All with reversible editability
releases.summary: Merge all objects into the image while preserving exact output pixels and the ability to undo.

Verified: Native menu/keyboard flattening, resize-dialog shortcut suppression, Undo/Redo, native save and355200 unchanged clipboard pixels.

limitations: Flattening selected objects and the Resize Image flattening confirmation remain planned.

releases.title: Resize Canvas with precise placement
releases.summary: Add transparent space or crop unused raster area using absolute or relative dimensions and nine placement anchors.

Verified: Native absolute/relative expansion, placement, invalid input and cut-object rejection, Escape/Cancel/title close, Undo/Redo and saving.

releases.title: Compact Resize Image controls

Native percent Apply, Undo/Redo and save retain seven editable objects;144000 copied pixels match the shared renderer.
UI regression checks bounded anchoring and outside-click cancellation at two viewport sizes.

limitations: Print units, DPI metadata and resampling choices remain planned.

releases.title: Pixel grid for precise magnified editing

The toggle stays enabled below its visibility threshold and reports its state. Only visible grid lines are drawn.
Verified: Native 800% and panned 1600% viewing, hidden grid at 400%, menu and keyboard toggles, and shortcut suppression during a resize draft.
Native clipboard output remains identical to all 3072 original fixture pixels. View changes leave editable documents and Undo/Redo untouched.
Automated alignment checks cover multiple display densities and large panned images; a real UI input/painting regression verifies document and history preservation.

limitations: Grid state lasts for the current editor session. Saved preferences, snapping, alignment guides and background controls remain planned.

releases.title: Resize images and keep objects editable
releases.summary: Set image dimensions in pixels or percent, retain editable objects, and restore the previous size with Undo.

Added: Resize Image opens from the Image menu or the dimensions strip. Pixels and Percent support linked aspect ratio or independent width and height, with validation before Apply.
Original pixels remain available for Revert to Original. Resize, Undo/Redo and project persistence include dimensions and editable object geometry.
Improved: Source resampling handles transparency without bleeding hidden RGB into visible edges. Later resizes use the retained original image.
Cancel and nested-popup Escape preserve the document. Invalid sizes and unchanged dimensions do not consume history.
Verified: Native 640 × 400 to 320 × 200 resize, Undo/Redo, saved dimensions and all seven editable objects. Native clipboard matches all 64000 resized pixels.

limitations: Print units, DPI metadata, custom resampling choices, crop and Resize Canvas remain planned. The installed reference Resize dialog has not been inspected.

Resized projects require this version or later. Editable projects retain original pixels. Native Export file-picker inspection remains blocked.

releases.title: Verified solid-black redaction
releases.summary: Redact sensitive areas with verified opaque covering pixels in flattened output, with clearer controls and editable movement and undo.

Verified: Native reverse-direction drawing, movement, one-step Undo/Redo and saved geometry on an original color-grid fixture.
All 52671 covered pixels are opaque black and all 203329 outside pixels are unchanged, checked against an independently generated mask. Native Copy All matches all 256000 pixels.
Engine checks cover fractional boundaries, reverse selections, full-edge coverage, transparent source pixels, save/reopen and PNG output.

limitations: Editable projects intentionally retain the original image and editable objects. Share flattened PNG or clipboard output when original pixels must remain concealed.
This scope is opaque rectangular redaction. Blur, pixelation and automatic sensitive-data detection are not implemented.
Native Export file-picker inspection remains blocked. PNG verification uses the saved native project through the shared renderer; native clipboard output is directly verified.

releases.title: Restore the original image with one undoable action
releases.summary: Edit > Revert to Original removes editable annotations while keeping the original image intact, with Undo, Redo and normal unsaved-change protection.

Verified: Native revert, disabled state, Undo/Redo, unsaved replacement cancellation and save/reopen using a seven-object synthetic project.
Native Copy All matches all 256000 source pixels after revert and all 256000 annotated pixels after Undo.

limitations: This is ClipCraft's independent revert behavior. Snagit's detailed revert semantics still need direct comparison, so that broader roadmap item remains Needs verification.

Pixel grid, snapping, crop/resize, library history and full reference interface parity remain unfinished. Native Save As inspection is still blocked.

releases.title: Zoom and pan without changing your image
releases.summary: Fit the canvas, inspect actual pixels or zoom in for precise editing while keeping document geometry and exported pixels intact.

Verified: Native drawings at 25% and panned 200% save exact predicted image coordinates. A 40 by 20 screen-pixel drag at 200% moves an object by exactly 20 by 10 image pixels, with one-step Undo and Redo.

limitations: Pixel grid, canvas snapping, workspace backgrounds and persistent view preferences remain planned. Zoom choices are an original implementation; exact Snagit zoom behavior is not yet qualified.
